# 5. Deployment {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

Taking it to production.

## Exporting Models

A PyTorch `.pt` file is great for research, but slow in production.
Convert to optimized formats using the `export` mode!

::: {.panel-tabset}

### CLI
```bash
# Export to ONNX (Great for CPU)
yolo export model=best.pt format=onnx

# Export to OpenVINO (Intel) or TensorRT (Nvidia GPUs)
yolo export model=best.pt format=openvino
```

### Python
```python
from ultralytics import YOLO

model = YOLO("best.pt")
model.export(format="onnx")
model.export(format="openvino")
```

:::

*Docs Reference: [Export](https://docs.ultralytics.com/modes/export/)*

## Inference with Exported Models

You don't need complex deployment code to use your exported models. The Ultralytics API loads them just like a standard PyTorch `.pt` file!

::: {.panel-tabset}

### CLI
```bash
yolo predict model=best.onnx source="https://ultralytics.com/assets/bus.jpg"
```

### Python
```python
from ultralytics import YOLO

model = YOLO("best.onnx")
results = model.predict(source="https://ultralytics.com/assets/bus.jpg")
print(results[0].boxes) 
```

:::

*Docs Reference: [Predict with Exported Models](https://docs.ultralytics.com/modes/predict/)*
